clue.text: To catch facial hair is agony

parts.note: to catch a sound is to hear it
TACHE is British slang for a moustache

explanation.surface: Getting a beard or moustache snagged on something is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional anguish or grief is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Somewhat supportive of heroin addiction

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath and so supports the first

parts.note: H is slang shorthand for heroin
somewhat means a bit, giving A BIT

explanation.surface: Someone who is a little in favour of heroin is heading for a drug problem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supportive of' means placed underneath, so A BIT goes below H.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is slang for a drug dependency, as in a heroin habit.

clue.text: Split payment?

parts.note: read 'split' as a couple separating: the money one ex-spouse pays the other after a divorce

explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance paid after a marriage breaks up is a payment caused by a split.

clue.text: Banker hosting party, not entirely vagrant

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the banker's word holds the party's word

parts.note: a bank teller handles customers' cash

indicators.note: the party word loses its final letter, so it is not all there

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A bank clerk throws a party, though not a full one, for a homeless wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: A bank teller is the 'banker' here, not a riverbank; 'not entirely' trims the party to RAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in this sense is a wanderer of no fixed abode, much like a vagrant.

clue.text: Delivered a calm pronouncement, in focus

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: delivered means sent and calm means peace, so the phrase is 'sent a peace'

explanation.surface: Someone made a soothing statement while concentrating hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'sent a peace' sounds just like the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The central feature of a display or table is its main point of attention, its focus.

clue.text: Goal achieving result

definitions.meaning: an aim or purpose, as in the ... justifies the means
an outcome or conclusion, the way something finishes

explanation.surface: Reaching the target brings the desired outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aim one strives for and the final outcome of a process.

clue.text: Mature leopard's first to bare teeth

parts.note: to mature is to grow up

indicators.note: the opening letter of the big cat's name is taken

explanation.surface: A grown leopard is the first to show its fangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarling with teeth shown is what a menacing dog or cat does when it makes a low rumble.

clue.text: Rat on drugs

definitions.meaning: to rat is to inform on someone to the police

explanation.surface: Someone informs while high on narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang both for informing on criminals and for cannabis.

clue.text: Gold in case, diamonds in hole

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
if means in case, as in take a coat if it rains
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A gold ring in a box and jewels hidden in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to 'in case', not a container signal; the second is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening or aperture, a kind of hole.

clue.text: Famous psychedelic guru withholding information, died

indicators.note: to withhold is to hold back inside, so the guru's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Timothy Leary was the 1960s champion of LSD
GEN is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A well-known drug guru kept a secret and then passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: Timothy Leary was the American psychologist who promoted LSD in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary means celebrated or renowned, very famous.

clue.text: Country where girl's discarded?

indicators.note: the clue asks where the girl is put, signalling that her name goes inside the other word

parts.note: something discarded is thrown in the bin
Rita is a girl's name; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A nation in which young women are cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags the whimsy: a girl in the bin is one discarded, so 'where' places the girl's name inside the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is a country, the island containing England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Picture success as a transvestite?

indicators.note: being in the state of a transvestite means being in drag, so the success word is placed in that word

parts.note: a cross-dressing performer is said to be in drag
a success is a win

explanation.surface: A photo of a triumph by a cross-dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'a transvestite' is being in drag, so 'as a' puts WIN in DRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing is a picture made with pencil, pen or crayon.

clue.text: Valuable collection at limit of gaudiest range

indicators.note: the limit of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of gaudiest is taken

parts.note: to range is to wander or rove

explanation.surface: Treasures displayed at the far end of the flashiest line of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuable things, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: Concerned with unmarried woman, one getting on seeking lessening of pain

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters
Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
I is the Roman numeral one
on means proceeding, as in getting on with work

explanation.surface: An elderly single woman wants relief from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is a period when symptoms of a disease ease or diminish.

clue.text: Catching cold? Me Indian — me put right!

definitions.text: Catching cold? Me Indian — me put right!

indicators.note: catching means taking in, so the reworked letters close around the cold letter
putting something right means rearranging it into proper order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A tribal healer, catching a chill, says he must cure himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' shuffles INDIAN ME and 'Catching' takes in C to give DICINEMAN; the whole clue also pictures a healer curing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal healer in Native American tradition treats ailments such as a cold.

clue.text: Tree bark

definitions.meaning: the laurel, whose leaves are used in cooking
to bark or howl, as a hound does

explanation.surface: The rough outer covering of a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the laurel tree and also means a dog's deep howl.

clue.text: Primitive weapon, huge thing, an indicator of force

parts.note: boomer is slang for anything exceptionally large
G is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon described as enormous and a sign of strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick used by Aboriginal Australian hunters is an early weapon.

clue.text: Order airborne — dare pilot to break record held

indicators.note: the record is held inside the rearranged letters
to break something is to smash it apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A pilot is challenged to beat a record, with orders to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order airborne' is a taxonomic order of flying insects, not a command to take off; 'break' rearranges the fodder to LIDOPTERA, and the record goes in after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterflies and moths form a flying insect order of that scientific name.

clue.text: One driven to overtake green convertible

parts.note: to pass a car is to overtake it

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed, so the letters of green are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist overtakes a green open-top car.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone carried in a vehicle, driven by another.

clue.text: One's withdrawn from pound and Euro with firm backing — these things happen

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the firm abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: one is taken out of the word for monies

parts.note: the pound and the Euro are both currencies
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A single coin is taken out of circulation with a company's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns CO into OC; 'withdrawn from' removes I from CURRENCIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrences are events, things that happen.

clue.text: Greek character turning nose up at Italian offering

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
someone turning their nose up at something is against it, anti

explanation.surface: A Greek turns up his nose at food from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, something Italy has to offer.

clue.text: Spring plant that's tropical making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the plant's name is read backwards

parts.note: the yam is a tropical climbing plant with edible tubers

explanation.surface: A tropical plant reappears in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: May is a month in the spring season.

clue.text: Watery Earth orbits Sun, which is hot

indicators.note: a planet that orbits circles round, so the mud word goes around the star word

parts.note: mud is earth mixed with water
the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A wet planet circles its sun, which gives off heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is not the abbreviation S here: the sun is a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a hot-tasting condiment, something with a fiery bite.

clue.text: Long runner, an expert on food

parts.note: an epic is something very long
the Ure is a Yorkshire river; a runner is a river in crosswords

explanation.surface: A marathon athlete happens to be a gourmet.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a connoisseur devoted to fine food and drink.

clue.text: Distressed having to spend time keeping quiet

indicators.note: the first pieces keep the quiet letter inside them

parts.note: to spend money or effort is to use it
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy at having to pass the time in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' holds P inside USE-T, after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as an adjective means troubled or distressed.

clue.text: Follow station to the west, not to east at first

indicators.note: the east letter goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: in an across clue going to the west means reading right to left, backwards
not means without, so the word to is removed

parts.note: Euston is a London railway terminus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions telling a traveller to follow the line west from a station, not east.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON, a London railway station, loses TO ('not to') to give EUSN; 'to the west' turns it to NSUE; E goes 'at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a result.

clue.text: Guard's heading off to gain access

indicators.note: the guard word loses its first letter

parts.note: a sentry is a guard; the 's makes the guard's heading

explanation.surface: A sentry goes off to get inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry means the right or means of getting in, access.

clue.text: Elephants won't suffer such men being trampled in India etc

indicators.note: the rearranged men go inside the continent

parts.note: India and its neighbours are in Asia

indicators.note: trampled things are crushed out of shape, so men is rearranged

explanation.surface: Men are trampled by elephants in India and nearby countries.
explanation.walkthrough: Elephants are said never to forget, so they never suffer memory loss; 'such' is a link. 'being trampled' turns MEN into MNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, and elephants proverbially never forget.

clue.text: One fired from branch

definitions.meaning: a firearm, something a shot is fired from
an offshoot, as in a branch of the ... forces or a tree limb

explanation.surface: A man is sacked by a local office.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a weapon and a subsidiary branch of an organisation.

clue.text: Shout after plane, one leaving the country

indicators.note: the shouting word comes after the plane

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: Someone yells after boarding a flight out of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant moves from one country to another.

clue.text: Sparkle left in drink, close to flat

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the drink

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A glass of spirits left out goes flat in the light.
explanation.definitionFit: A glint is a small flash or sparkle of light.

clue.text: Assistant offering mother and father aid, collapsing in city

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York
FR is the abbreviation for father, a priest's title

indicators.note: collapsing things fall into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A helper offers his parents assistance as things fall apart in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' turns FR AID into FRIDA; Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Man Friday is a loyal personal aide, after Crusoe's servant.
